content:
Apple is widely expected to launch a new touchscreen MacBook Pro later this month. This will be the first Mac ever to feature a touchscreen, and Apple is also laying the groundwork in macOS 27.2 to support touch gestures.

Apple today released macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers, which includes new code related to upcoming touchscreen interaction features. As discovered by Aaron Perris of MacRumors, several built-in Apple apps have added "Gesture Recognizers":

  • Photos added "PXGTouchDwellGestureRecognizer"
  • Notes added "ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer"
  • Safari added "a touch sentinel recognizer"
  • Quick Look added "dragTouch feature"

macOS 27.2 beta 3 also adds new long-press animation effects to the Dock, which could also be a hint at the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro:

Apple has been gradually making changes to macOS 27 to prepare for touchscreen support, including the first-ever pull-to-refresh feature. macOS 27 also adds touch input support for Sidecar, allowing users to use an iPad as an external display for their Mac.

Bloomberg has also reported on Apple's work on optimizing macOS for the upcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro. For example, when tapping buttons or controls, macOS will dynamically display relevant touch options; similarly, tapping the menu bar will automatically enlarge controls for easier touch operation.

In addition to the touchscreen, the new MacBook Pro is reportedly set to feature an OLED display and will be "noticeably lighter" than current models.

Apple is expected to release the new MacBook Pro later this month (or perhaps MacBook Ultra?), though Bloomberg has noted there is a chance it could be delayed until November.
